This guide uses the package's example data to estimate a four-cluster model.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
data <- mmgsem::data_example
```

## Fit the measurement model

The measurement model is estimated using `lavaan`:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
S1_model <- '
    F1 =~ V1 + V2 + V3 + V4 + V5
    F2 =~ V6 + V7 + V8 + V9 + V10
    F3 =~ V11 + V12 + V13 + V14 + V15
    F4 =~ V16 + V17 + V18 + V19 + V20
'

MM_fit <- lavaan::cfa(
  model         = S1_model,
  data          = data,
  group         = "group",
  group.equal   = "loadings",
  group.partial = c("F1 =~ V2",
                    "F2 =~ V7",
                    "F3 =~ V12",
                    "F4 =~ V17")
)
```

## Fit the structural model

The structural model is then clustered by `mmgsem()`:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
S2_model <- '
    F4 ~ F1 + F3
    F3 ~ F1 + F2
'

mmgsem_fit <- mmgsem::mmgsem(
  dat     = data,
  S1      = S1_model,
  S2      = S2_model,
  group   = "group",
  nclus   = 4,
  seed    = 1,
  s1_type = "lavaan",
  s1_fit  = MM_fit
)

summary(mmgsem_fit)
print(mmgsem_fit$posteriors)
```

## Select the number of clusters

`ModelSelection()` fits each cluster count in the range specified by `nclus`.
Its computation can take considerably longer than fitting a single model.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
modelSelection_fit <- mmgsem::ModelSelection(
  dat     = data,
  S1      = S1_model,
  S2      = S2_model,
  group   = "group",
  nclus   = c(1, 6),
  seed    = 1,
  s1_type = "lavaan",
  s1_fit  = MM_fit
)

summary(modelSelection_fit, model_selection = TRUE)
selected_fit <- mmgsem::extract(object = modelSelection_fit, nclus = 4)
```

## Compute standard errors

Computing standard errors uses numerical differentiation and can take a long
time, especially for larger models. Run this step when you need standard
errors; precomputed standard errors for this example data are also available.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# standard_errors <- mmgsem::standard_errors
standard_errors <- mmgsem::compute_se(object = selected_fit)
summary(selected_fit, se = standard_errors)
```

## Longitudinal example

For longitudinal data, `lmmgsem()` tracks clusters (latent states) across
time. Supply a long-format data frame with group and time columns and the same
observed indicators at each group-time combination. Every group must have
observations at every time point, with at least two time points. Replace
`longitudinal_data` below with your data; adapt the measurement and structural
model syntax if your indicators or model differ.

The measurement and structural models from the cross-sectional example can be
reused:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
mi_results <- mmgsem::compute_mi_long_stepwise_score(
  data = longitudinal_data,
  model = S1_model,
  group_var = "group",
  time_var = "time",
  method = "test_statistic",
  specific_noninv = FALSE
)
s1_fit <- mi_results$final_fit
```

This estimates a measurement model in which each group-time combination is
treated as a separate group. Alternatively, omit `s1_fit` below to have
`lmmgsem()` estimate the measurement-invariance model automatically.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
lmmgsem_fit <- mmgsem::lmmgsem(
  dat = longitudinal_data,
  S1 = S1_model,
  S2 = S2_model,
  group = "group",
  time = "time",
  nclus = 4,
  seed = 1,
  s1_fit = s1_fit
)

summary(lmmgsem_fit)
```

To compare longitudinal models with different numbers of states, include
`time` in `ModelSelection()`. The range must not exceed the number of groups.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
longitudinal_selection <- mmgsem::ModelSelection(
  dat = longitudinal_data,
  S1 = S1_model,
  S2 = S2_model,
  group = "group",
  time = "time",
  nclus = c(1, 4),
  seed = 1
)

summary(longitudinal_selection, model_selection = TRUE)
selected_longitudinal_fit <- mmgsem::extract(
  longitudinal_selection,
  nclus = 4
)
```

Standard errors for `lmmgsem()` are not currently implemented.
